summary: Two Spring Boot services and Postgres on EKS write ordinary log lines through one log pattern setting that prints %X{trace_id}. The run first has no agent, then the OpenTelemetry Java agent attached through one environment variable. The lab reads trace IDs from the real logs, asks Splunk APM for each one, and counts how many open a trace.
expected: reproduce.sh prints no agent settings, the jar's SHA-256, the log pattern, log lines read and zero lines with an ID, then HERO_RESULT: reproduced.

files.content:
# Jump from any Java log line to its Splunk APM trace, with zero code

## What it shows

A small Spring Boot system runs on EKS: `orders` calls `inventory`, and `inventory` reads Postgres. Both use the same jar on the same image, and each writes ordinary log lines through SLF4J and Logback.

One log pattern setting prints the ID the agent places in Logback's MDC:

```yaml
- name: LOGGING_PATTERN_CORRELATION
  value: "[trace_id=%X{trace_id:-none} span_id=%X{span_id:-none}] "
```

That setting is on in both runs, so the OpenTelemetry Java agent is the only difference between them.

* `reproduce.sh` (BEFORE): installs the Splunk OTel Collector, builds the jar once in the cluster, runs it with no agent, and counts log lines and lines carrying an ID.
* `fix.sh` (BUILD): sets `JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS` on each service and runs the same load. While the load runs it reads a trace ID from a real log line every 2 seconds, in turn from each service, and asks Splunk for each one at `/v2/apm/trace/<id>/latest`.

An ID counts as opened when that API returns at least one span for it. The load sends no trace header, so each ID comes from the agent and is known only through the logs.

The output holds three counts (log lines read, lines carrying an ID, IDs opened), the seconds from each ID's log timestamp to its first readable trace, and one real log line with the spans of its trace.

`otel.javaagent.logging` stays at its default. The lab doesn't need `otel.javaagent.logging=application`, and `check.sh` tries it once and prints what happens.

Application log export is off, because this lab sends to Observability Cloud only and reads the logs from the pods. Traces use the agent's defaults.

## Run it

Set `AWS_REGION`, `LAB_NAME`, `TF_VAR_lab_name` (the same value as `LAB_NAME`), `SPLUNK_REALM`, `SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN` (ingest) and `SPLUNK_API_TOKEN` (read). Then run:

```bash
terraform init && terraform apply -auto-approve
./reproduce.sh
./fix.sh
./cleanup.sh
terraform destroy -auto-approve
```

The run uses two `t3.large` nodes and an EKS control plane for about an hour. The seconds to a readable trace come from the lab runner's clock and each node's log clock, on one cluster and one load rate.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The free check, run on a GitHub runner with Docker before AWS is paid for. It uses the lab's own source, images, agent, log pattern
# and load script. The agent prints its spans here, so each trace ID read from a log line is matched to a span the agent exported.
# Kubernetes and Splunk are not part of this check.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
mkdir -p c/src c/out c/init c/load

python3 - <<'PY'
import re
def block(path, key):
    text = open(path).read()
    m = re.search(rf"^  {re.escape(key)}: \|\n((?:    .*\n|\n)+)", text, re.M)
    return "\n".join(line[4:] for line in m[1].splitlines()) + "\n"
open("c/src/pom.xml", "w").write(block("k8s/00-build.yaml", "pom.xml"))
open("c/src/App.java", "w").write(block("k8s/00-build.yaml", "App.java"))
open("c/init/init.sql", "w").write(block("k8s/10-app.yaml", "init.sql"))
open("c/load/load.py", "w").write(block("k8s/20-load.yaml", "load.py"))
text = open("k8s/10-app.yaml").read()
open("c/pattern.txt", "w").write(re.search(r'name: LOGGING_PATTERN_CORRELATION, value: "([^"]+)"', text)[1])
PY

IMAGE=$(grep -m1 -oE 'maven:[^ ]+' k8s/10-app.yaml)
PY_IMAGE=$(grep -m1 -oE 'python:[^ ]+' k8s/20-load.yaml)
PG_IMAGE=$(grep -m1 -oE 'postgres:[^ ]+' k8s/10-app.yaml)
AGENT_URL=$(grep -m1 -oE 'https://github.com/[^"]+\.jar' k8s/00-build.yaml)
PATTERN=$(cat c/pattern.txt)
echo "log pattern from the manifest: $PATTERN"
docker network create lab >/dev/null

echo "== Fetching the agent and building the jar"
docker run --rm -v "$PWD/c/out:/lab" "$PY_IMAGE" python -c "
import time, urllib.request
for attempt in range(12):
    try:
        urllib.request.urlretrieve('$AGENT_URL', '/lab/opentelemetry-javaagent.jar'); break
    except Exception as e:
        print('retrying the download:', e); time.sleep(10)
else:
    raise SystemExit('the agent could not be downloaded')"
docker run --rm -v "$PWD/c/src:/src:ro" -v "$PWD/c/out:/lab" "$IMAGE" sh -c '
  set -e; mkdir -p /w/src/main/java/lab; cp /src/pom.xml /w/; cp /src/App.java /w/src/main/java/lab/; cd /w
  mvn -q -B -DskipTests package; cp target/app.jar /lab/app.jar'
ls -l c/out

docker run -d --name postgres --network lab -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=lab -v "$PWD/c/init:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d:ro" "$PG_IMAGE" >/dev/null
for i in $(seq 1 30); do docker exec postgres pg_isready -U postgres >/dev/null 2>&1 && break; sleep 1; done
sleep 3

start() {   # name, JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS
  docker run -d --name "$1" --network lab -v "$PWD/c/out:/lab:ro" --entrypoint java \
    -e SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL=jdbc:postgresql://postgres:5432/postgres -e SPRING_DATASOURCE_USERNAME=postgres \
    -e SPRING_DATASOURCE_PASSWORD=lab -e INVENTORY_URL=http://inventory:8080 -e "JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS=$2" \
    -e "LOGGING_PATTERN_CORRELATION=$PATTERN" "$IMAGE" -Xms256m -Xmx256m -jar /lab/app.jar >/dev/null
}
ready() {
  for i in $(seq 1 60); do docker logs "$1" 2>&1 | grep -q 'process running for' && break; sleep 1; done
  docker logs "$1" 2>&1 | grep -q 'process running for' || { docker logs "$1" 2>&1 | tail -30; echo "CHECK FAILED: $1 didn't start"; exit 1; }
}
load() { docker run --rm --name load --network lab -v "$PWD/c/load:/load:ro" -e "SECONDS_TOTAL=$1" -e SECONDS_WARM=2 "$PY_IMAGE" python /load/load.py; }
hasid() { grep -cE 'trace_id=[0-9a-f]{32}' "$1" || true; }

echo "== No agent"
start inventory ""
start orders ""
ready inventory
ready orders
load 20 | tee c/before.txt
grep -q 'errors=0' c/before.txt || { docker logs orders 2>&1 | tail -30; echo "CHECK FAILED: requests failed with no agent"; exit 1; }
{ docker logs orders 2>&1; docker logs inventory 2>&1; } > c/before-logs.txt
grep -m2 ' lab\.App' c/before-logs.txt
BEFORE_LINES=$(grep -c ' lab\.App' c/before-logs.txt || true)
BEFORE_IDS=$(hasid c/before-logs.txt)
echo "request lines with no agent: $BEFORE_LINES"
echo "lines with an id with no agent: $BEFORE_IDS"
docker rm -f orders inventory >/dev/null

echo "== With the agent, printing the spans it exports"
for s in inventory orders; do
  start "$s" "-javaagent:/lab/opentelemetry-javaagent.jar -Dotel.service.name=$s -Dotel.traces.exporter=console -Dotel.metrics.exporter=none -Dotel.logs.exporter=none"
done
ready inventory
ready orders
load 20 | tee c/after.txt
grep -q 'errors=0' c/after.txt || { docker logs orders 2>&1 | tail -30; echo "CHECK FAILED: requests failed with the agent"; exit 1; }
sleep 8
docker logs orders > c/orders.txt 2>&1
docker logs inventory > c/inventory.txt 2>&1
cat c/orders.txt c/inventory.txt > c/agent.log
grep -m1 'opentelemetry-javaagent - version' c/agent.log || true

# Application lines only. The span printout holds the same IDs, so it must not count as a log line.
grep -v LoggingSpanExporter c/agent.log > c/app.log
grep LoggingSpanExporter c/agent.log > c/spans.log
READ=$(grep -c . c/app.log || true)
WITH_ID=$(hasid c/app.log)
REQUESTS=$(grep -c ' lab\.App' c/app.log || true)
WARN=$(grep ' lab\.App' c/app.log | grep WARN | grep -cE 'trace_id=[0-9a-f]{32}' || true)
grep ' lab\.App' c/app.log | grep -E 'trace_id=[0-9a-f]{32}' | awk '!seen[$0]++' > c/lines.txt
grep -oE 'trace_id=[0-9a-f]{32}' c/lines.txt | cut -d= -f2 | awk '!seen[$0]++' > c/ids.txt
TOTAL=$(grep -c . c/ids.txt || true)
STEP=$(( TOTAL / 40 )); [ "$STEP" -ge 1 ] || STEP=1
awk -v s="$STEP" 'NR % s == 0' c/ids.txt | head -40 > c/sample.txt
SAMPLED=$(grep -c . c/sample.txt || true)
MATCHED=0; SPAN_MATCHED=0; BOTH=0
while read -r id; do
  grep -qF "$id" c/spans.log && MATCHED=$(( MATCHED + 1 ))
  span=$(grep -m1 "trace_id=$id" c/lines.txt | grep -oE 'span_id=[0-9a-f]{16}' | cut -d= -f2)
  grep -F "$id" c/spans.log | grep -qF "${span:-none}" && SPAN_MATCHED=$(( SPAN_MATCHED + 1 ))
  grep -q "trace_id=$id" c/orders.txt && grep -q "trace_id=$id" c/inventory.txt && BOTH=$(( BOTH + 1 ))
done < c/sample.txt

echo "-- one log line and the spans of its trace"
ONE=$(head -1 c/sample.txt)
grep -m1 "trace_id=$ONE" c/lines.txt | cut -c1-190
grep -F "$ONE" c/spans.log | sed -E 's/^.*LoggingSpanExporter - //' | cut -c1-100

echo "log lines read: $READ"
echo "request lines: $REQUESTS"
echo "lines with an id: $WITH_ID"
echo "warn lines with an id: $WARN"
echo "ids sampled: $SAMPLED"
echo "ids matched to an exported trace: $MATCHED"
echo "ids whose log span_id is in that trace: $SPAN_MATCHED"
echo "ids in both services: $BOTH"
echo "FREE CHECK HEADLINE: $MATCHED of $SAMPLED log trace IDs match a trace the agent exported"
docker rm -f orders inventory >/dev/null

echo "== otel.javaagent.logging=application, tested once and not used by the lab"
for s in inventory orders; do
  start "$s" "-javaagent:/lab/opentelemetry-javaagent.jar -Dotel.javaagent.logging=application -Dotel.service.name=$s -Dotel.traces.exporter=console -Dotel.metrics.exporter=none -Dotel.logs.exporter=none"
done
TESTED=1
for s in inventory orders; do
  for i in $(seq 1 60); do docker logs "$s" 2>&1 | grep -q 'process running for' && break; sleep 1; done
  docker logs "$s" 2>&1 | grep -q 'process running for' || TESTED=0
done
if [ "$TESTED" = 1 ]; then
  load 6 | tail -2 || true
  sleep 7
  docker logs orders 2>&1 | grep -m3 -iE 'opentelemetry|otel|javaagent' | cut -c1-170 || true
  echo "with that setting, lines with an id: $(docker logs orders 2>&1 | grep -v LoggingSpanExporter | grep -cE 'trace_id=[0-9a-f]{32}' || true)"
  echo "with that setting, spans printed: $(docker logs orders 2>&1 | grep -c 'LoggingSpanExporter\|SERVER \[tracer' || true)"
else
  echo "with that setting the services did not reach the started line in 60 seconds"
fi
docker logs orders 2>&1 | grep -m1 -iE 'unrecognized|unknown|invalid' | cut -c1-170 || true

[ "$BEFORE_LINES" -gt 0 ] && [ "$BEFORE_IDS" -eq 0 ] || { echo "CHECK FAILED: the run with no agent should log requests and carry no ID"; exit 1; }
[ "$WITH_ID" -gt 0 ] && [ "$WITH_ID" -eq "$REQUESTS" ] || { echo "CHECK FAILED: $WITH_ID of $REQUESTS request lines carry an ID"; exit 1; }
[ "$SAMPLED" -ge 30 ] && [ "$MATCHED" -eq "$SAMPLED" ] && [ "$SPAN_MATCHED" -eq "$SAMPLED" ] || { echo "CHECK FAILED: not every sampled ID matched"; exit 1; }
[ "$BOTH" -eq "$SAMPLED" ] || { echo "CHECK FAILED: not every sampled ID appears in both services"; exit 1; }
echo "CHECK PASSED"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Never fail hard. Nothing here creates AWS resources outside Terraform.
set +e
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
name=$(terraform output -raw cluster_name 2>/dev/null)
if [ -n "$name" ]; then
  aws eks update-kubeconfig --name "$name" --region "$AWS_REGION" >/dev/null 2>&1
  if kubectl --request-timeout=15s get nodes >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    timeout 180 helm uninstall splunk-otel-collector -n splunk --timeout 120s >/dev/null 2>&1
    timeout 120 kubectl delete namespace demo splunk --wait=false >/dev/null 2>&1
    echo "cleanup: helm release uninstalled, namespaces deleting"
  else
    echo "cleanup: cluster not reachable, nothing to remove"
  fi
else
  echo "cleanup: no cluster output, nothing to remove"
fi
exit 0

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# BUILD: the OTel Java agent, attached through one environment variable. Same jar, image, Collector and log pattern, no code change.
# Then read trace IDs from the application logs while the load runs, and ask Splunk for each one.
set -uo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"

START=$(date +%s)
LIMIT=830
SAMPLE=40        # one log line every 2 seconds, in turn from each service, across the whole load
HERO_DONE=0
remaining() { echo $(( START + LIMIT - $(date +%s) )); }
cap() { local want=$1 reserve=$2 r; r=$(( $(remaining) - reserve )); [ "$r" -lt 5 ] && r=5; [ "$want" -lt "$r" ] && echo "$want" || echo "$r"; }
emit() { HERO_DONE=1; echo "HERO_RESULT: $1"; }
fail() { echo "FAIL: $*"; [ "$HERO_DONE" = 1 ] || emit not_fixed; exit 0; }
trap '[ "$HERO_DONE" = 1 ] || { HERO_DONE=1; echo "HERO_RESULT: not_fixed"; }' EXIT

aws eks update-kubeconfig --name "$(terraform output -raw cluster_name)" --region "$AWS_REGION" >/dev/null || fail "could not write kubeconfig"
[ -n "${SPLUNK_REALM:-}" ] || fail "SPLUNK_REALM is not set"
[ -n "${SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN:-}" ] || fail "SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN is not set"
[ -n "${SPLUNK_API_TOKEN:-}" ] || fail "SPLUNK_API_TOKEN is not set"
API="https://api.${SPLUNK_REALM}.signalfx.com"
LOAD_NODE=$(cat load-node.txt) || fail "no load node recorded"

newest() { kubectl -n demo get pods -l "app=$1" --field-selector=status.phase=Running --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp -o name | tail -1; }
series() { curl -sS --max-time 20 -G -H "X-SF-Token: $SPLUNK_API_TOKEN" "$API/v2/metrictimeseries" --data-urlencode "query=$1" --data-urlencode "limit=1000" 2>/dev/null; }

# "Opened" means exactly this: the trace API returned at least one span for that ID.
opened() { jq -e 'type == "array" and length >= 1' "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; }

get_trace() {   # id, file. Prints the HTTP status.
  curl -sS --max-time 15 -o "$2" -w '%{http_code}' -H "X-SF-Token: $SPLUNK_API_TOKEN" "$API/v2/apm/trace/$1/latest" 2>/dev/null
}

watch_id() {   # id, service, log time. Asks every 5 seconds and records the first time the trace can be read.
  local id=$1 service=$2 logged=$3 n code now
  for n in $(seq 1 100); do
    [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$DEADLINE" ] || return 0
    code=$(get_trace "$id" "traces/$id.tmp")
    echo "$code" >> api-codes.txt
    if opened "traces/$id.tmp"; then
      now=$(date +%s.%3N)
      mv "traces/$id.tmp" "traces/$id.json"
      awk -v i="$id" -v s="$service" -v a="$now" -v b="$logged" 'BEGIN{printf "%s %s %.1f\n", i, s, a-b}' >> ready.txt
      return 0
    fi
    sleep 5
  done
}

echo "== 2. The before-check: the cluster's own data reaches Splunk"
cluster=0
t0=$(date +%s)
limit=$(cap 150 500)
while [ $(( $(date +%s) - t0 )) -lt "$limit" ]; do
  cluster=$(series "k8s.cluster.name:${LAB_NAME}" | jq -r '.count // (.results | length) // 0' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
  [ "${cluster:-0}" -gt 0 ] && break
  sleep 15
done
echo "cluster metric time series in Splunk: ${cluster:-0}"
[ "${cluster:-0}" -gt 0 ] || fail "no cluster data reached Splunk, so a zero below would prove nothing"

echo "== 3. The whole change: one environment variable on each service"
for s in orders inventory; do
  kubectl -n demo set env "deployment/$s" "JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS=-javaagent:/lab/opentelemetry-javaagent.jar -Dotel.service.name=$s -Dotel.exporter.otlp.endpoint=http://\$(HOST_IP):4318 -Dotel.resource.attributes=deployment.environment=$LAB_NAME,deployment.environment.name=$LAB_NAME -Dotel.logs.exporter=none" >/dev/null || fail "could not set the variable on $s"
done
why() { kubectl -n demo get pods -o wide | tail -8 | cut -c1-120; kubectl -n demo get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | tail -10 | cut -c1-180; }
kubectl -n demo rollout status deploy/inventory --timeout="$(cap 120 400)s" >/dev/null || { why; fail "inventory did not roll out"; }
kubectl -n demo rollout status deploy/orders --timeout="$(cap 120 400)s" >/dev/null || { why; fail "orders did not roll out"; }

for s in orders inventory; do
  p=$(newest "$s")
  echo "$s image: $(kubectl -n demo get "$p" -o jsonpath='{.spec.containers[0].image}')"
  echo "$s jar: $(kubectl -n demo exec "$p" -c app -- sha256sum /lab/app.jar)"
  kubectl -n demo logs "$p" -c app 2>/dev/null | grep -m1 'opentelemetry-javaagent - version' | sed "s/^/$s /"
done
same=$(kubectl -n demo exec "$(newest orders)" -c app -- sha256sum /lab/app.jar | awk '{print $1}')
[ "$same" = "$(cat jar-sha.txt)" ] && echo "jar unchanged from the before run" || fail "the jar changed, so the comparison would be unfair"
orders_pod=$(newest orders)
inventory_pod=$(newest inventory)

echo "== 4. The same load, reading trace IDs from the logs as it runs"
mkdir -p traces lines
: > sample.txt; : > ready.txt; : > api-codes.txt
DEADLINE=$(( $(date +%s) + $(cap 540 70) ))
kubectl -n demo delete pod load --ignore-not-found --wait=true >/dev/null 2>&1
sed "s/LOAD_NODE/$LOAD_NODE/" k8s/20-load.yaml | kubectl apply -f - >/dev/null || fail "could not start the load"
kubectl -n demo wait pod/load --for=condition=Ready --timeout="$(cap 60 300)s" >/dev/null || { why; fail "the load did not start"; }
for n in $(seq 1 "$SAMPLE"); do
  if [ $(( n % 2 )) = 1 ]; then service=orders; pod=$orders_pod; else service=inventory; pod=$inventory_pod; fi
  line=$(kubectl -n demo logs "$pod" -c app --since=3s 2>/dev/null | grep ' lab\.App' | grep -E 'trace_id=[0-9a-f]{32}' | tail -1)
  id=$(grep -oE 'trace_id=[0-9a-f]{32}' <<<"$line" | cut -d= -f2)
  if [ -n "$id" ] && ! grep -q "^$id " sample.txt; then
    logged=$(date -d "${line%% *}" +%s.%3N 2>/dev/null) || logged=""
    if [ -n "$logged" ]; then
      echo "$id $service $logged" >> sample.txt
      echo "$line" > "lines/$id.txt"
      watch_id "$id" "$service" "$logged" >/dev/null 2>&1 &
    fi
  fi
  sleep 2
done
kubectl -n demo wait pod/load --for=jsonpath='{.status.phase}'=Succeeded --timeout="$(cap 60 200)s" >/dev/null || { kubectl -n demo logs load --tail=20; fail "the load did not finish"; }
kubectl -n demo logs load | tee load-after.txt
grep -q 'errors=0' load-after.txt || echo "the load reported failed requests"

echo "== 5. Waiting for Splunk, once, until every sampled trace can be read or the window ends"
for n in $(seq 1 110); do
  [ -z "$(jobs -r)" ] && break
  [ $(( n % 6 )) = 1 ] && echo "  $(grep -c . ready.txt || true) of $(grep -c . sample.txt || true) readable after $(( $(date +%s) - START ))s of this script"
  sleep 5
done
kill $(jobs -pr) 2>/dev/null
wait 2>/dev/null
rm -f traces/*.tmp

echo "== 6. Everything the logs hold, counted from the finished files"
kubectl -n demo logs "$orders_pod" -c app > logs-orders.txt 2>/dev/null
kubectl -n demo logs "$inventory_pod" -c app > logs-inventory.txt 2>/dev/null
cat logs-orders.txt logs-inventory.txt > logs-all.txt
read_lines=$(grep -c . logs-all.txt || true)
with_id=$(grep -cE 'trace_id=[0-9a-f]{32}' logs-all.txt || true)
request_lines=$(grep -c ' lab\.App' logs-all.txt || true)
warn_lines=$(grep ' lab\.App' logs-all.txt | grep -E 'WARN' | grep -cE 'trace_id=[0-9a-f]{32}' || true)
sampled=$(grep -c . sample.txt || true)
ids_open=0; both=0; codes=""
while read -r id service logged; do
  [ -f "traces/$id.json" ] && opened "traces/$id.json" && ids_open=$(( ids_open + 1 ))
  grep -q "trace_id=$id" logs-orders.txt && grep -q "trace_id=$id" logs-inventory.txt && both=$(( both + 1 ))
done < sample.txt

echo "-- trace API answers, by HTTP status"
sort api-codes.txt | uniq -c | awk '{print "api status " $2 ": " $1 " calls"}'

echo "-- every sampled ID, with the seconds from its log timestamp to the first readable trace"
while read -r id service logged; do
  r=$(grep "^$id " ready.txt | awk '{print $3}')
  echo "TIMING $id $service ${r:-still_arriving_when_the_window_ended}"
done < sample.txt

echo "-- one real log line and its trace, for the picture"
pick=$(awk '{print $1}' ready.txt | head -1)
for id in $(awk '$2 == "orders" {print $1}' ready.txt); do pick=$id; break; done
if [ -n "$pick" ]; then
  code=$(get_trace "$pick" picture.json)        # read again now, so spans that arrived after the first read are included
  opened picture.json || cp "traces/$pick.json" picture.json
  span=$(grep -oE 'span_id=[0-9a-f]{16}' "lines/$pick.txt" | cut -d= -f2)
  cp "lines/$pick.txt" picture-line.txt
  echo "PICTURE_LOG_LINE: $(cat "lines/$pick.txt")"
  jq -c '.[] | del(.tags, .processTags, .logs)' picture.json | cut -c1-420 | sed 's/^/PICTURE_SPAN: /'
  echo "spans in the picture trace: $(jq 'length' picture.json)"
  echo "services in the picture trace: $(jq -c '[.[].serviceName] | unique' picture.json)"
  echo "log line span_id $span appears in this trace: $(jq --arg s "$span" '[.[] | select(.spanId == $s)] | length' picture.json)"
fi

median=$(awk '{print $3}' ready.txt | sort -n | awk '{a[NR]=$1} END{if (NR) print (NR%2 ? a[(NR+1)/2] : (a[NR/2]+a[NR/2+1])/2)}')
slowest=$(awk '{print $3}' ready.txt | sort -n | tail -1)

echo
echo "log lines read: ${read_lines:-0}"
echo "HERO_MEASURE: log_lines_read=${read_lines:-0}"
echo "request lines: ${request_lines:-0}"
echo "HERO_MEASURE: request_lines=${request_lines:-0}"
echo "lines with an id: ${with_id:-0}"
echo "HERO_MEASURE: lines_with_id=${with_id:-0}"
echo "warn lines with an id: ${warn_lines:-0}"
echo "HERO_MEASURE: warn_lines_with_id=${warn_lines:-0}"
echo "ids sampled: ${sampled:-0}"
echo "HERO_MEASURE: ids_sampled=${sampled:-0}"
echo "ids opened: ${ids_open:-0}"
echo "HERO_MEASURE: ids_opened=${ids_open:-0}"
echo "ids in both services: ${both:-0}"
echo "HERO_MEASURE: ids_in_both_services=${both:-0}"
if [ -n "$median" ]; then
  echo "seconds to readable median: $median"
  echo "HERO_MEASURE: seconds_to_readable_median=$median"
  echo "seconds to readable slowest: $slowest"
  echo "HERO_MEASURE: seconds_to_readable_slowest=$slowest"
fi

# The headline can be anything from the run. The result only asks that the logs gave IDs and Splunk opened at least one after the wait,
# so lag can change the number shown but not this line.
if [ "${with_id:-0}" -gt 0 ] && [ "${sampled:-0}" -ge 10 ] && [ "${ids_open:-0}" -ge 1 ]; then
  emit fixed
else
  emit not_fixed
fi

apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: db-init
  namespace: demo
data:
  init.sql: |
    create table stock (id int primary key, sku text not null, qty int not null);
    insert into stock select i, 'SKU-' || i, 100 + i from generate_series(1, 100) i;

apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: load
  namespace: demo
data:
  load.py: |
    # Sends one order request every 50 ms. It sets no trace header, so every trace ID comes from the agent and is found only in the logs.
    import http.client, os, random, sys, time
    seconds, warm = int(os.environ["SECONDS_TOTAL"]), int(os.environ["SECONDS_WARM"])
    conn, took, errors, gap = http.client.HTTPConnection("orders", 8080, timeout=10), [], 0, 0.05
    start = time.time()
    while time.time() - start < seconds:
        sent = time.time()
        try:
            conn.request("GET", "/orders/%d" % random.randint(1, 1000))
            r = conn.getresponse(); r.read()
            ok = r.status == 200
        except Exception:
            ok = False
            conn.close()
        ms = (time.time() - sent) * 1000
        if not ok:
            errors += 1
        elif sent - start >= warm:
            took.append(ms)
        time.sleep(max(0, gap - ms / 1000))
    took.sort()
    if not took:
        print("LOAD no successful requests after warm-up, errors=%d" % errors)
        sys.exit(1)
    print("LOAD requests=%d errors=%d p50_ms=%.2f p95_ms=%.2f" % (len(took), errors, took[len(took) // 2], took[int(len(took) * 0.95)]))
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: load
  namespace: demo
spec:
  restartPolicy: Never
  nodeName: LOAD_NODE
  volumes:
    - name: load
      configMap:
        name: load
  containers:
    - name: load
      image: python:3.12-slim
      command: ["python", "/load/load.py"]
      env:
        - { name: SECONDS_TOTAL, value: "90" }
        - { name: SECONDS_WARM, value: "30" }
      volumeMounts:
        - { name: load, mountPath: /load }

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# BEFORE: a Spring Boot orders service calls an inventory service, which reads Postgres. The Collector runs, and no agent is attached.
# The log pattern already asks for %X{trace_id}, so the agent is the only change between this run and fix.sh.
set -uo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"

START=$(date +%s)
LIMIT=810
HERO_DONE=0
remaining() { echo $(( START + LIMIT - $(date +%s) )); }
cap() { local want=$1 reserve=$2 r; r=$(( $(remaining) - reserve )); [ "$r" -lt 5 ] && r=5; [ "$want" -lt "$r" ] && echo "$want" || echo "$r"; }
emit() { HERO_DONE=1; echo "HERO_RESULT: $1"; }
fail() { echo "FAIL: $*"; [ "$HERO_DONE" = 1 ] || emit not_reproduced; exit 0; }
trap '[ "$HERO_DONE" = 1 ] || { HERO_DONE=1; echo "HERO_RESULT: not_reproduced"; }' EXIT

aws eks update-kubeconfig --name "$(terraform output -raw cluster_name)" --region "$AWS_REGION" >/dev/null || fail "could not write kubeconfig"

echo "== 1. Waiting for 2 worker nodes"
ready=0
t0=$(date +%s)
while [ $(( $(date +%s) - t0 )) -lt 300 ]; do
  ready=$(kubectl --request-timeout=15s get nodes --no-headers 2>/dev/null | grep -c ' Ready' || true)
  [ "${ready:-0}" -ge 2 ] && break
  sleep 10
done
kubectl --request-timeout=15s get nodes -o wide || true
[ "${ready:-0}" -ge 2 ] || fail "nodes did not become Ready"
kubectl -n kube-system rollout status deploy/coredns --timeout="$(cap 90 500)s" || true

# The app stays on one node and the load generator on the other, in both runs.
APP_NODE=$(kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}')
LOAD_NODE=$(kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[1].metadata.name}')
echo "$APP_NODE" > app-node.txt
echo "$LOAD_NODE" > load-node.txt
echo "app node: $APP_NODE"
echo "load node: $LOAD_NODE"

[ -n "${SPLUNK_REALM:-}" ] || fail "SPLUNK_REALM is not set"
[ -n "${SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN:-}" ] || fail "SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN is not set"

echo "== 2. Installing the Splunk OTel Collector (chart 0.163.1) first, so it is running in both runs"
helm repo add splunk-otel-collector-chart https://signalfx.github.io/splunk-otel-collector-chart >/dev/null 2>&1
helm repo update >/dev/null 2>&1
helm upgrade --install splunk-otel-collector splunk-otel-collector-chart/splunk-otel-collector \
  --version 0.163.1 --namespace splunk --create-namespace \
  --set splunkObservability.realm="$SPLUNK_REALM" \
  --set splunkObservability.accessToken="$SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  --set clusterName="$LAB_NAME" \
  --set cloudProvider=aws \
  --set distribution=eks \
  >/dev/null || fail "collector install failed"
kubectl -n splunk rollout status daemonset/splunk-otel-collector-agent --timeout="$(cap 150 500)s" || fail "collector agent not ready"

echo "== 3. Building the jar in the cluster, once, and fetching the agent, unused for now"
sed "s/APP_NODE/$APP_NODE/" k8s/00-build.yaml | kubectl apply -f - >/dev/null || fail "could not start the build"
state=""
t0=$(date +%s)
limit=$(cap 430 300)
while [ $(( $(date +%s) - t0 )) -lt "$limit" ]; do
  state=$(kubectl -n demo get job build -o jsonpath='{.status.conditions[?(@.status=="True")].type}' 2>/dev/null)
  case "$state" in *Complete*|*Failed*) break ;; esac
  sleep 10
done
kubectl -n demo logs job/build --all-containers --tail=20 2>/dev/null || true
case "$state" in *Complete*) ;; *) kubectl -n demo describe job build | tail -15; fail "the build did not finish: ${state:-still running}" ;; esac
echo "build took $(( $(date +%s) - t0 ))s"

echo "== 4. Deploying Postgres, orders and inventory with no agent"
sed "s/APP_NODE/$APP_NODE/" k8s/10-app.yaml | kubectl apply -f - >/dev/null || fail "could not deploy the app"
kubectl -n demo rollout status deploy/postgres --timeout="$(cap 90 200)s" || fail "postgres did not start"
kubectl -n demo rollout status deploy/inventory --timeout="$(cap 120 180)s" || fail "inventory did not start"
kubectl -n demo rollout status deploy/orders --timeout="$(cap 120 170)s" || fail "orders did not start"

newest() { kubectl -n demo get pods -l "app=$1" --field-selector=status.phase=Running --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp -o name | tail -1; }

echo "== 5. No agent is attached, the log pattern is set, and the image and jar are recorded"
for s in orders inventory; do
  p=$(newest "$s")
  echo "$s image: $(kubectl -n demo get "$p" -o jsonpath='{.spec.containers[0].image}')"
  echo "$s JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS or OTEL settings: $(kubectl -n demo get "$p" -o json | jq '[.spec.containers[0].env[].name | select(test("^(JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS|OTEL_)"))] | length')"
  echo "$s log pattern: $(kubectl -n demo get "$p" -o json | jq -r '.spec.containers[0].env[] | select(.name == "LOGGING_PATTERN_CORRELATION") | .value')"
  echo "$s jar: $(kubectl -n demo exec "$p" -c app -- sha256sum /lab/app.jar)"
done
kubectl -n demo exec "$(newest orders)" -c app -- sha256sum /lab/app.jar | awk '{print $1}' > jar-sha.txt

echo "== 6. The same load as the agent run: one request every 50 ms"
kubectl -n demo delete pod load --ignore-not-found --wait=true >/dev/null 2>&1
sed "s/LOAD_NODE/$LOAD_NODE/" k8s/20-load.yaml | kubectl apply -f - >/dev/null || fail "could not start the load"
kubectl -n demo wait pod/load --for=jsonpath='{.status.phase}'=Succeeded --timeout="$(cap 170 15)s" || { kubectl -n demo logs load --tail=20; fail "the load did not finish"; }
kubectl -n demo logs load | tee load-before.txt
grep -q 'errors=0' load-before.txt || fail "requests failed"

echo "== 7. What the logs carry with no agent"
for s in orders inventory; do kubectl -n demo logs "$(newest "$s")" -c app > "before-$s.txt" 2>/dev/null; done
cat before-orders.txt before-inventory.txt > before-all.txt
grep ' lab\.App' before-all.txt | tail -2
read_lines=$(grep -c . before-all.txt || true)
request_lines=$(grep -c ' lab\.App' before-all.txt || true)
with_id=$(grep -cE 'trace_id=[0-9a-f]{32}' before-all.txt || true)
echo "log lines read before: ${read_lines:-0}"
echo "request lines before: ${request_lines:-0}"
echo "lines with an id before: ${with_id:-0}"
echo "HERO_MEASURE: log_lines_read_before=${read_lines:-0}"
echo "HERO_MEASURE: lines_with_id_before=${with_id:-0}"
[ "${request_lines:-0}" -gt 0 ] || fail "the services wrote no request lines"

emit reproduced
